home_title_paragraph: An Irish name coming from the word ‘fia’ which means ‘deer’, representing the words 'wild/free', is a free, bilingual (English/Irish) web application designed as an all-in-one business toolkit for emerging and early-career freelance artists in Ireland.

hub_subtitle: Guides, links and support for freelance artists in Ireland.
hub_tax_desc: If you earn income as a freelance artist in Ireland, you are legally required to register as a sole trader with Revenue. You can do this online via MyAccount. Registration is free and takes around 10 minutes.
hub_vat_desc: As a freelance artist, you must register for VAT only if your annual income exceeds €40,000 for services. Cultural services may qualify for VAT exemptions worth checking.
hub_self_assess_desc: Self-employed people in Ireland file a Form 11 each year by 31 October. Your income minus allowable expenses is your taxable profit. Keep receipts for everything.
hub_exemption_desc: Revenue operates an artists' exemption allowing qualifying creative work to be exempt from income tax up to €50,000 per year. Applies to original, creative work in categories including visual art, writing and music.
hub_arts_council_desc: The main government body for funding the arts in Ireland. Offers bursaries, project awards and travel grants for individual artists at all career stages. Check their opportunities calendar regularly.
hub_local_funding_desc: Local Enterprise Offices (LEOs) across Ireland offer small business grants, mentoring, and training. Some programmes specifically target creative sector applicants.
hub_creative_industries_desc: Creative Ireland's Creativity Fund and Screen Ireland both support project-based creative work. Deadlines vary; sign up for their newsletters to stay informed.
hub_copyright_desc: In Ireland, copyright is automatic from the moment you create original work. You do not need to register. Copyright generally lasts 70 years after the creator's death under the Copyright and Related Rights Act 2000.
hub_moral_rights_desc: As an artist you hold moral rights to be identified as the creator of your work and to object to derogatory treatment. These rights exist separately from economic copyright and cannot be sold, only waived.
hub_contracts_title: Why You Need a Written Contract
hub_contracts_desc: A written contract protects both you and your client. It should clearly state the scope of work, payment terms, deadlines, revision limits, and who owns the final work. Fiadh includes a contract template generator.
hub_pricing_minimum_desc: Visual Artists Ireland and Create Ireland publish recommended minimum fees for artists working with publicly funded organisations. These are a useful baseline even for private commissions.
hub_formula_title: How to Calculate Your Hourly Rate
hub_formula_desc: A simple starting point: add up your annual living costs and business expenses, divide by the number of billable hours you realistically work per year (typically 1,000 to 1,400 for freelancers), then add a profit margin.
hub_negotiation_title: Asking for What You Are Worth
hub_negotiation_desc: It is normal to feel uncomfortable quoting prices. Remember: your price includes your skill, time, equipment, and expertise built over years. Send a written quote before starting any work.
hub_advocacy_desc: Create is the national development agency for collaborative arts. Offers resources, advocacy, peer support, and professional development opportunities.
hub_visual_art_desc: The national membership body for visual artists in Ireland. VAI supports visual artists through practical resources, a legal helpline, peer groups and the VAI Opportunities bulletin with current calls and commissions.
hub_community_desc: An informal community resource thread collating advice on pricing, contracts, difficult clients, and self-employment shared by working artists.
hub_welfare_desc: Ireland's pilot Basic Income for the Arts scheme runs until 2025. Check gov.ie for outcomes and any successor scheme announcements.
